newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav PM confident of sanctions lifting.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav PM confident of sanctions lifting.

text.p: Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic on Tuesday said his government expected U.N. economic sanctions to be completely lifted this week.

"We rightfully expect from the international community to finally lift sanctions during the current week, in accordance with the Dayton peace accord," Kontic said, opening a series of specialised international fairs in Belgrade.

Some sanctions, imposed in May 1992 to punish Belgrade for its support to Bosnian Serbs, were suspended by the U.N. Security Council last November as a follow-up to the U.S.-initiated Balkan peace accords signed in Dayton, Ohio last year.
A council resolution stipulated the sanctions would be lifted entirely 10 days after the Bosnian elections, which took place on September 14.

But the United States has interpreted the resolution as saying the 10-day countdown should begin after the the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), certified the Bosnian elections were fair. That has not happened yet.

The United States has said previously it would keep a so-called outer ring of sanctions, such as barring the rump Yugoslav state of Serbia and Montenegro from institutions like the International Monetary Fund. Washington can block Belgrade's participation in some of these institutions unilaterally.

Kontic said "there is not one serious reason to keep the so-called outer ring of sanctions and prevent Yugoslavia from returning to the United Nations, International Monetary Fund, World Bank, OSCE and other international institutions.

"Yugoslavia's return to the world scene would not only be a recognition for its crucial contribution to the peace process ... but also a big step towards strengthening peace and stability in the region," Kontic said.
According to the Prime Minister, the presence of over 70 foreign companies at the fair signals their readiness to restore business ties with Yugoslav firms.
"It is clear why they want to find a place on our market in time, because a period of rapid economic development, modernisation and restructuring is ahead of us," he said.
Kontic said that the Yugoslav economy was successfully recovering from the sanctions.

Economic performance was encouraging, Kontic said, adding that the industrial output grew over past nine months at about five percent on the average, with chances to improve during the last quarter of the year.
The government's recent contacts with international organisations, other governments, including former Yugoslav republics, pave way to wide cooperation and development, he said.

"But for a serious development we would need financial and other help," he said, adding "there were real chances to develop for those who preserved personnel, technology and organisational skills and who can respond to new demands." -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
